classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught elimination method to obtain two launch angles, then substitute into time and velocity equations and interpret the velocity direction.

content.prompt: A particle is projected with initial speed $50\text{ m/s}$. On its flight it passes through a point $P$ at horizontal distance $100\text{ m}$ and vertical distance $25\text{ m}$ from the point of projection.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the angle of projection $\alpha$ is $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)$ or $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac92\right)$.

answer.worked:
Using $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$, the equations of motion are
$$\begin{aligned}x&=50\cos\alpha\,t,\\y&=50\sin\alpha\,t-5t^2.\end{aligned}$$
At $P$, $x=100$:
$$\begin{aligned}50\cos\alpha\,t&=100,\\t&=\frac{2}{\cos\alpha}.\end{aligned}$$
Substitute into the vertical equation with $y=25$:
$$\begin{aligned}50\sin\alpha\left(\frac{2}{\cos\alpha}\right)-5\left(\frac{4}{\cos^2\alpha}\right)&=25,\\100\tan\alpha-20\sec^2\alpha&=25,\\100\tan\alpha-20(1+\tan^2\alpha)&=25,\\20\tan^2\alpha-100\tan\alpha+45&=0,\\4\tan^2\alpha-20\tan\alpha+9&=0,\\(2\tan\alpha-1)(2\tan\alpha-9)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Hence $\tan\alpha=\frac12$ or $\tan\alpha=\frac92$, giving
$$\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)\quad\text{or}\quad\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac92\right).$$

children.label: i
children.prompt: the time to reach $P$ (give exact values and approximations to 1 d.p.),

answer.short: For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)$: $t=\sqrt5\text{ s}\approx2.2\text{ s}$. For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac92\right)$: $t=\sqrt{85}\text{ s}\approx9.2\text{ s}$.
answer.worked:
For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)$, $\cos\alpha=\frac{2}{\sqrt5}$:
$$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{2}{\cos\alpha}\\&=\frac{2}{2/\sqrt5}\\&=\sqrt5\text{ s}\\&\approx2.2\text{ s}.\end{aligned}$$
For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac92\right)$, $\cos\alpha=\frac{2}{\sqrt{85}}$:
$$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{2}{\cos\alpha}\\&=\frac{2}{2/\sqrt{85}}\\&=\sqrt{85}\text{ s}\\&\approx9.2\text{ s}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: the velocity at $P$ (to 1 d.p. where necessary).

answer.short: For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)$: $44.7\text{ m/s}$ horizontally forwards. For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac92\right)$: $44.7\text{ m/s}$ at $76.0^\circ$ below the horizontal.
answer.worked:
The velocity components are $\dot{x}=50\cos\alpha$ and $\dot{y}=50\sin\alpha-10t$.

For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)$, $\sin\alpha=\frac1{\sqrt5}$, $\cos\alpha=\frac2{\sqrt5}$ and $t=\sqrt5$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dot{x}&=50\cos\alpha\\&=\frac{100}{\sqrt5}\\&=20\sqrt5,\\\dot{y}&=50\sin\alpha-10t\\&=\frac{50}{\sqrt5}-10\sqrt5\\&=10\sqrt5-10\sqrt5\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The velocity is $20\sqrt5\text{ m/s}\approx44.7\text{ m/s}$ horizontally forwards. Since $\dot{y}=0$, $P$ is the point of maximum height.

For $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac92\right)$, $\sin\alpha=\frac9{\sqrt{85}}$, $\cos\alpha=\frac2{\sqrt{85}}$ and $t=\sqrt{85}$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dot{x}&=50\cos\alpha\\&=\frac{100}{\sqrt{85}},\\\dot{y}&=50\sin\alpha-10t\\&=\frac{450}{\sqrt{85}}-10\sqrt{85}\\&=\frac{450-850}{\sqrt{85}}\\&=-\frac{400}{\sqrt{85}}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Speed}&=\sqrt{\dot{x}^{\,2}+\dot{y}^{\,2}}\\&=\sqrt{\frac{100^2+400^2}{85}}\\&=20\sqrt5\text{ m/s}\\&\approx44.7\text{ m/s}.\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal component is positive and the vertical component is negative, so the direction is below the forward horizontal:
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{400}{100}\right)\\&=\tan^{-1}(4)\\&\approx76.0^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The velocity is $44.7\text{ m/s}$ at $76.0^\circ$ below the horizontal.
